A 1697 Dutch memorandum on Jaffnapatam condemns the failed elephant-hunting arrangement, orders improved elephant transport and care, regulates auctions, taxes, trade, labor, slavery, fortifications, courts, supplies, and public works, and strengthens Dessave de Bitter’s authority.

In the adventure story, John Hartley travels from London to New York, abducts Althea from Mrs. Mordaunt’s house, and takes her by cab to Donovan’s Brooklyn saloon, where she is confined upstairs. Dan tracks her, disguises himself as an Italian street musician, discovers her location, enters Donovan’s bar-room, rescues Althea, and traps Donovan in the cellar. Hartley is later arrested for forged railway certificates; Harriet Vernon adopts Dan and reunites the family.

In the later novel, Croyden and Macloud search Greenberry Point and its adjoining Bay for Parmenter’s buried treasure, fail, and return to Hampton. Croyden meets a blackmailer outside Clarendon, arms Moses in the library, and later discovers disguised intruders searched the house. Elaine Cavendish visits Miss Carrington at Ashburton to meet Croyden, while Macloud arranges the visit. Croyden unexpectedly recovers financially when Elaine secretly buys his worthless Virginia Development bonds.
